Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the action to commence on Day 3. Tim Southee leads his troops out to the middle and they are followed by the two openers of South Africa. It will be the skipper, Neil Brand to open the innings alongside Clyde Fortuin. Tim Southee has the new ball in hand and he is raring to go. Let's play...

On the other hand, New Zealand started Day 2 strongly, not allowing the Proteas to go past 250. William O'Rourke was the star of the show for them, as the debutant went on to pick four wickets. In reply, Kane Williamson, Tom Latham, Rachin Ravindra, and Will Young got starts but failed to convert into something substantial. Neil Wagner, with a few lusty blows, helped the hosts get close to parity, but in general, the Kiwi batting performance left a lot to be desired. The onus will fall on the Kiwi pacers and Rachin Ravindra to keep the opposition to a manageable total here in the second inning. Will New Zealand hit back? We shall find out soon, as the first ball on Day 3 is not far away.

Having started the day with an overnight score of 222 and four wickets in hand, South Africa were pushing for a big total, but they just could not get going. As a result, they were bowled out for 242 inside the first 45 minutes of play. With the ball, the Proteas were a different side and kept hitting the right areas consistently. Dane Piedt led the charge for them, registering his career-best figures of 5 for 89 to help the visitors take a 31-run lead. Now, it will be important for their batters to see off that first hour and press on the advantage once it gets easier to bat.

Hello and a warm welcome, folks, to our coverage of Day 3 of the second Test between New Zealand and South Africa at Seddon Park in Hamilton. Day 2 witnessed a turnaround from the Proteas, and it was undoubtedly their best day of the tour. As we look ahead to the 'Moving Day', the visitors find themselves in front, not by much, and expect the hosts to come back strong.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

This is why we love Test cricket, don't we? The game ebbed and flowed throughout the day and it will be South Africa who will be the happier of the two sides. Not many would have expected them to be in this position but their grit and determination has given them the upper hand in this Test. That said, the Proteas batters will have a tough task first up on the 'Moving Day' where they will have to avoid losing early wickets. On the other hand, New Zealand will have to put this batting performance behind them and fight their way back into the game with the ball. The action on Day 3 will commence at 3.30 am IST (10 pm GMT, the previous day) but our build-up will begin much sooner. Until then, take care and cheers!

As for New Zealand, they will be disappointed with their batting effort. At one stage, it looked like they would get past South Africa's 242, but it went horribly wrong for them in the third session. New Zealand's batting effort started on the wrong foot as Devon Conway got out for a duck. Kane Williamson and Tom Latham got starts and looked for a good score until both were dismissed in their forties. The young guns, Rachin and Will Young, batted with intent to negotiate the tricky phase before Tea. Rachin was tentative outside the off-stump, and after his departure, it all went downhill for the Kiwis. Will Young tried to slog his way out of trouble but could not succeed, leaving the tail to get them close to parity. Neil Wagner fought a lone fight and counterattacked to reduce the deficit, and he did a fine job at it. Thanks to his 33-run knock, New Zealand conceded a 31-run first-inning lead, which might well have been over 50 had Wagner not come to their rescue.

SESSION SUMMARY - 90 runs, 29.3 overs, and 9 wickets. A sensational bowling performance from South Africa to bowl New Zealand out for 211. The visitors take a lead of 31 runs, a significant one given the context of the game, and that will also be STUMPS on DAY 2. The Proteas did not start the day on a strong note, but their fighting spirit has ensured that they have ended the day holding the ascendancy. South Africa began the day with the hope of getting close to 300. The debutant Shaun von Berg's early dismissal hindered their progress, leaving Ruan de Swardt without ample support from the tail. As a result, the visitors lost their last four wickets for just 15 runs to be bundled out for 242. Despite an inauspicious start to the day, the visitors were able to start well with the ball, thanks mainly to Dane Paterson. After Lunch, they were made to wait until Dane Piedt's twin strikes brought them right back into it. The visitors looked flat at the start of the third session until Tshepo Moreki gave them a breakthrough, and they never looked back since. Dane Piedt and his namesake Dane Paterson kept chipping away at the wickets and piled on the misery on the Kiwis. Piedt ended with a five-wicket haul, his first one in 9 years while Paterson took 3 and Moreki had one to his name.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the third and final session. South Africa are in a huddle near the ropes before they spread out to take their respective field positions. They are followed by the two Kiwi batters, Will Young and Rachin Ravindra. Tshepo Moreki is at the top of his mark and he is raring to go. Here we go...

Will Young and Rachin Ravindra took a few deliveries to settle in and assess the pace of the pitch and once they got an idea the duo took every scoring opportunity and managed to score a good clicks. Will Young in particular walked out with a positive frame of mind while Rachin Ravindra grew along nicely. The stage is set for both these Kiwi batters to take the game away from the Proteas by playing big innings and cementing their spot in the Test side. The Protea bowlers would be looking up to Dane Paterson and Dane Piedt specifically for breakthrough as they have looked like the best bowlers by far on this surface.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the afternoon session on Day 2. The two umpires make their way out to the middle as do the players. Kane Williamson and Tom Latham in readiness to resume their innings. It will be Dane Paterson to kick things off with the ball. Let's play...
... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

On the other hand, South Africa were hopeful of pushing their first-innings total close to 300 with two batters at the crease who looked in control late on Day 1. They were dealt an early blow in the form of Shaun von Berg, who could only add four runs to his overnight score. The tail was unable to lend Ruan de Swardt the support he needed, resulting in the visitors only adding 22 runs to their overnight score to be bowled out for 242. With the ball, Dane Paterson gave them the early wicket they were after. Tshepo Moreki and Dane Piedt were disciplined as well to keep things tight and build the pressure even more. It will be important for South Africa to sustain this pressure for long periods and not allow easy scoring for the Kiwi batters. Will they succeed in doing so? Join us back at 6.10 am IST (12.40 am GMT) for the post-Lunch session to find out.

SESSION SUMMARY - 49 runs, 24.2 overs and 5 wickets. New Zealand will be happy to go in at Lunch with just one causality and the first session has gone their way. New Zealand started Day 2 in exactly the manner they would have hoped for. William O'Rourke helped the Kiwis open one end by dismissing Shaun von Berg before going on to clean up the tail with Tim Southee. In reply, the hosts were rocked early, losing Devon Conway for a duck. Tom Latham and Kane Williamson were challenged upfront with the new ball by the Proteas pacers and offie Dane Piedt. They absorbed the pressure and saw through that phase to go to Lunch with only one wicket down, trailing by 215 runs.
